name: Berkeley Mono
classification_notes: Purpose-built as a monospaced coding typeface with humanist sans-serif undertones, Berkeley Mono sits squarely in the mono category rather than a general-purpose sans.
summary: A humanist monospace built by a software engineer for software engineers, tuned for code rather than adapted from a text face.
description: Berkeley Mono treats the machine-readable typefaces of 1970s computing as a design brief rather than a nostalgia trip, pairing that objectivity with humanist sans-serif proportions for genuine legibility. Version 2 runs 12 weights across 5 widths and 2 slants, with variable fonts covering all three axes, plus over 150 ligatures for those who want them. Built and tested against real production code throughout its development.
foundry_blurb: U.S. Graphics Company describe Berkeley Mono as a love letter to the golden era of computing, engineered for reading and writing code with excellent legibility and glyphs that are distinct without being distracting.
